settings.help.title: Help & FAQ
settings.help.intro: How identity, hubs and your data actually work here — and what to do when something goes sideways.
settings.help.faq.identity_home.a: In this browser, on this device. Your key is derived from your 24 recovery words and never leaves it: a hub only ever sees the public half. There is no account on a server, no email, no password — which is also why an identity does not follow you to another browser, another device, or another hub's page unless you bring it there yourself.
settings.help.faq.browser_wipe.q: What happens if I clear my browser data?
settings.help.faq.browser_wipe.a: You lose this browser's copy of the key, not the identity. Paste the 24 words back (or import your .wavvon-backup file) and the same identity returns, byte for byte. Your hub list comes back too, as long as you have a home hub: it travels in an encrypted blob stored there, and only your phrase opens it. What you never wrote down and never exported is gone for good — nobody holds a copy, the hub operator included.
settings.help.faq.secure_account.q: How do I put my account beyond reach of an accident?
settings.help.faq.secure_account.a:
1. Write the 24 words on paper and keep them somewhere other than this device.
2. Settings → Manage accounts → download the .wavvon-backup file, protected by a passphrase you choose, and keep it in your password manager.
3. Settings → Manage accounts → Home hubs: check that at least one hub is listed. That is where your encrypted settings and hub list are stored.
settings.help.faq.same_client.q: Why should I always come back to the same page?
settings.help.faq.same_client.a: Every hub serves its own copy of the Wavvon client from its own address, and a browser keeps stored data separate per address. The client itself is multi-hub, though: from a single page you can add, switch between and talk to as many hubs as you like. So pick the page where you set your identity up, bookmark it, and add every other hub from there — one identity in one place, instead of a different one per hub.
settings.help.faq.invite_landing.q: I clicked an invite and it asks me to create an identity. Now what?
settings.help.faq.invite_landing.a: You landed on that hub's own page, which knows nothing about the identity you set up elsewhere. Don't create a second one. Instead: open your usual Wavvon page, choose Add hub, and paste the whole invite link — the code travels with it. If you would rather move in here for good, import your .wavvon-backup file, bearing in mind you then have the same identity in two places, each with its own local hub list.
settings.help.faq.home_hub.a: The hub that holds what is about you rather than about a community: your device list, your settings, your DM inbox, and the encrypted copy of your hub list. The first hub you sign in to becomes your home hub automatically, and you can change it or add more — it is a list, so any one of them being down is survivable. A hub you run yourself is the privacy-conscious answer: nothing stops you from putting your own first and a community one behind it as a fallback.
settings.help.faq.operator_sees.q: What can a hub operator see?
settings.help.faq.operator_sees.a: Your public key, whatever you post in that hub's channels, and metadata about your personal state — how many devices you have, when messages arrive. Your settings and your hub list are encrypted on this device before they are uploaded, with a key derived from your phrase: the hub stores bytes it cannot read. Choosing a home hub is a trust decision, and hosting one yourself is the answer if you would rather not make it.
settings.help.faq.lost_everything.q: I lost both the phrase and the backup file.
settings.help.faq.lost_everything.a: Then that identity is not recoverable. It is a key, not an account: there is no password to reset and nobody holds a copy. What is left is creating a new identity and asking each hub's admins to hand your standing back on the new key — a human decision on their side. Some hubs let you nominate recovery contacts in advance who can then vouch for you; if yours does, it is in Settings.
settings.help.alpha_disclaimer: Wavvon is alpha software. Formats can still change in ways that break stored data, and nothing here is guaranteed to survive an update. Keep your phrase and your backup file safe, and don't put anything irreplaceable in yet.
